chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Dawood ibn Qasim al-Ja'fari who said:

I was with Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) when he said: When the Qaim rises, he will demolish the minarets and maqsoorahs that are in the mosques. I said to myself: For what reason is this? He turned to me and said: The meaning of this is that they are innovations, newly invented; neither a Prophet nor a Hujjah built them.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim (the Rising One), a title for the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.حُجَّةٌ: The Hujjah (Proof of God, often referring to the Imams)
key_terms.وَالْمَقَاصِيرَ: And the maqsoorahs (plural of maqsurah, enclosed areas in mosques)

ai.seo_question: Why will the Qaim demolish minarets and maqsoorahs according to Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) identifies the minarets and maqsoorahs as later architectural innovations (*bid'ah*) lacking precedent from the Prophet or the Imams, signaling their removal upon the rise of the Qaim. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on purifying worship spaces from non-traditional additions to restore the simplicity of early Islamic practice. The critique underscores the distinction between essential religious structures and culturally adopted embellishments.
